summary: Jamaica beat Canada 3-2 at BMO Field in Toronto in the second leg of the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal. The 4-4 aggregate tie sent Jamaica through on away goals to the semifinal and to Copa America 2024. Canada led through Alphonso Davies, but Shamar Nicholson's two goals and a Bobby De Cordova-Reid penalty turned the tie around. Canada must now beat Trinidad and Tobago in a March playoff to reach Copa America.
one_line: Jamaica won 3-2 in Toronto, progressing on away goals after a 4-4 aggregate tie to reach the Nations League semifinal and Copa America 2024.
key_facts: Jamaica won 3-2 at BMO Field in Toronto, their first-ever victory on Canadian soil, and the two legs finished 4-4 on aggregate.
Jamaica advanced on away goals to the CONCACAF Nations League semifinal and qualified for Copa America 2024.
Alphonso Davies opened the scoring for Canada on 25 minutes when his shot was saved onto the crossbar and spun in on the goal line, making it 3-1 on aggregate.
Shamar Nicholson scored twice for Jamaica, in the 63rd and 66th minutes by the report's goal list, within about three minutes of each other, to level the aggregate at 3-3.
Ismael Kone's header in the 69th minute made it 2-2 on the night and gave Canada a one-goal aggregate lead.
Stephen Eustaquio's handball in the box gave Jamaica a penalty, which Fulham's Bobby De Cordova-Reid converted in the 78th minute for the winner.
Jamaica's Demarai Gray was sent off in the 84th minute for a second yellow card for dissent, but Jamaica held on through nine minutes of stoppage time.
Jamaican goalkeeper Andre Blake made several saves, including two from Cyle Larin, to keep Jamaica in the tie in the first half.
Leon Bailey, the Aston Villa winger, hit the crossbar in the 48th minute with a shot that bounced on the line.
Canada will play Trinidad and Tobago in a one-off playoff in March to try to reach Copa America 2024, to be hosted in the U.S.
Jamaica were without West Ham striker Michail Antonio, who suffered an ACL injury in the first leg, and Gray started as striker in his place.
The referee was Cesar Ramos of Mexico, with kickoff at 7:30 p.m. local time on November 21, 2023.
The match was streamed on OneSoccer in Canada (available on Fubo) and on Paramount+ in the United States.
